title: Difficulties in the diagnosis of spinal hemorrhage – a multicentric retrospective study of risk factors
summary:
Bleeding in the spinal cord canal area is very rare and the exact frequency of this disease is unknown. Patients with these diseases usually have bilateral leg weakness, bilateral arm and leg weakness and/or a disorder of urinary and stool control.
The symptoms can be very different and at first you may only notice weakness on one side of the body. Then there is the possibility that a stroke will initially be thought of when presenting to the hospital. To date, there are only individual case reports and small case series as well as review articles on this topic. Studies on a larger number of patients are lacking. This is intended to be made possible within the framework of this study.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
all patients with the diagnosis: spinal hemorrhage or ICD 10 code: G95.10
Exclusion criteria:
Previous spinal surgery within the last 3 months
Traumatic spinal hemorrhage
